text: In 1857, the Company gave its Indian soldiers a new rifle.
To load it, you had to bite open a paper cartridge.
The cartridges were greased with cow and pig fat, offensive to both Hindus and Muslims.
At Meerut in May, soldiers who refused the cartridges were jailed.
Their comrades rose up, freed them, and marched to Delhi.
There they declared the old, powerless Mughal emperor, Bahadur Shah Zafar, the ruler of
The revolts spread across North India.
In Chhansi, a young queen, Rani Lakshmibai, led her troops into battle on horseback and
died fighting. The British crushed the rising with terrible brutality. Whole villages were
burned. Rebels were tied to cannons and blown apart. Bahadur Shah Zafar was exiled to Rangoon
in Burma. The Mughal dynasty, after 330 years, was over. And the British government decided
the company could not be trusted with India anymore. In 1858, the British crown took over directly.
The British Raj had begun. Your Majesty, India is now ruled by the crown.
Splendid. And the company closed, Your Majesty. Then I shall need a new title.
